DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Position [L4].** Jesus Christ had a mother, Mary, and no human biological father. His conception was the work of the Holy Ghost, and Joseph stood to him as husband of his mother and legal father only. By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed generated the child. The case runs from the text's own verbs, prepositions and pronouns.

## 1. Matthew's genealogy stops "begat" at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** In Matthew 1:2-16 every link uses ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, G1080, "begat, fathered"). The last link does not. Joseph is called ἀνήρ (*anēr*, G435, "husband"), and the birth is "of whom" (ἐξ ἧς, *ex hēs*), with ἐκ (*ek*, G1537) meaning "out of, from the source" and the relative pronoun feminine singular. Jesus came out of Mary, not out of Joseph.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:12 shows the writer uses "begat" freely: "Jechonias begat Salathiel". Where he means a father's generation he says so. At Joseph he changes the construction.

**[L4]** Two footings carry this: the repeated verb in Matthew 1:12 and the verb and feminine pronoun in Matthew 1:16 [L2]. The writer who writes "begat" thirty-nine times declines it at the last link, and he assigns the birth to the woman by gender. So the genealogy is a legal line through Joseph and not a claim of generation by him.

## 2. The conception preceded the coming together, and its source was the Holy Ghost

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, G4905) means "to come together" as husband and wife. The text places the pregnancy before that. The source is ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (*ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit").

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** γεννηθέν (*gennēthen*, G1080, "begotten, conceived") is the same root as "begat" in the genealogy. The angel assigns the begetting of the child to the Holy Ghost, with the same preposition ἐκ ("out of").

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

**[L2]** ἐγίνωσκεν (*eginōsken*, G1097, "knew") is the verb for sexual knowledge. Joseph did not know her through to the birth.

**[L4]** The three verses give a chain. Pregnancy came before any coming together (Matthew 1:18, *synelthein*). The begetting is from the Holy Ghost (Matthew 1:20, *ek*). Joseph did not know her until the birth (Matthew 1:25, *eginōsken*). So no male act of Joseph's, nor any other man's, entered the conception.

## 3. Mary says "I know not a man," and the angel names the agent

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω (*andra ou ginōskō*, "a man I do not know") is her stated reason for asking. The angel answers with two verbs: ἐπελεύσεται (*epeleusetai*, G1904, "shall come upon") and ἐπισκιάσει (*episkiasei*, G1982, "shall overshadow"). Both name the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as agent. No man is named.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." The Greek is παρθένος (*parthenos*, G3933, "virgin"). It quotes Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." The Hebrew there is הָעַלְמָה (*ha-almah*, H5959, "the young woman of marriageable age, unmarried"). The same word stands in Genesis 24:43, "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water," of Rebekah, who is described in Genesis 24:16 as "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L4]** Mary's question rests on "I know not a man" [L1, Luke 1:34]. The angel supplies an agent that is not a man [L1, Luke 1:35]. Matthew applies *parthenos* to the conception [L3, Matthew 1:23]. So the angel's answer excludes a man's contribution by what it supplies in place of one.

## 4. Fatherhood of God is not physical generation, and the text separates Joseph's role

**[L1]** John 4:24: "God is a Spirit."

**[L3]** Luke 24:39: "a spirit hath not flesh and bones."

**[L4]** Both verses fix the nature of God as Spirit without flesh and bones [L1, L3]. So the begetting by the Holy Ghost in Matthew 1:20 cannot be a biological act. The word "father" for God means a divine origin, not a physical one. The child's flesh is attributed to the mother.

**[L1]** Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L2]** κατηρτίσω (*katērtisō*, from καταρτίζω, G2675, "to fit, prepare") says the body was prepared for him.

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."

**[L2]** γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός (*genomenon ek gynaikos*, "made out of a woman") names only the woman as source, with the same *ek* as in Matthew 1:16.

**Joseph's place.** **[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." **[L2]** ἐνομίζετο (*enomizeto*, G3543, "was reckoned, supposed by custom") marks the relation as a supposition and not a fact of generation. **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." **[L3]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" The child corrects the term "father" and applies it to God. Luke 2:33 shows the narrator's own usage: "Joseph and his mother marvelled." The narrator does not call Joseph his father. **[L4]** The footings are the *enomizeto* of Luke 3:23 [L2] and the child's own correction in Luke 2:49 [L3]. Joseph's "fatherhood" is legal and reputed. It is not biological.

## 5. The Davidic line is secured without Joseph's seed

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L2]** σπέρματος (*spermatos*, G4690, "seed") and κατὰ σάρκα (*kata sarka*, "according to the flesh") fix a bodily descent from David. The Holy Ghost is not a David descendant, so the descent must come through the mother.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:12 puts Joseph in the line of Jechonias. Jeremiah 22:30 says of him: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David." The Hebrew זֶרַע (*zera*, H2233, "seed") is the same word as in Genesis 3:15: "thy seed and her seed."

**[L4]** The footings are *spermatos kata sarka* in Romans 1:3 [L2] and the *zera* sentence in Jeremiah 22:30 [L3]. Jesus is of David's seed in the flesh without being the seed of Jechonias through Joseph. That resolves the apparent conflict only if the flesh came from Mary. Luke 1:32 gives "the throne of his father David" by legal succession through Joseph, as Matthew 1:20 addresses him: "Joseph, thou son of David".

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew's genealogy breaks the "begat" pattern at Joseph. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16 "of whom was born Jesus" with [L2] ἐγέννησεν (*egennēsen*, "begat") against ἐξ ἧς (*ex hēs*, "out of whom," feminine), and [L3] Matthew 1:12 "Jechonias begat Salathiel" showing that the writer uses "begat" where he means fathering.
2. The conception preceded any coming together of Joseph and Mary and was from the Holy Ghost. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together" with [L2] συνελθεῖν (*synelthein*, "to come together") and ἐκ (*ek*, "out of"), [L1] Matthew 1:20, and [L3] Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth".
3. Mary's "I know not a man" is answered by the Holy Ghost as agent, not a man. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34-35 with [L2] ἐπισκιάσει (*episkiasei*, "shall overshadow") and παρθένος (*parthenos*, "virgin"), and [L3] Matthew 1:23 and Isaiah 7:14.
4. God's fatherhood of the child is not physical generation, and Joseph's fatherhood is only reputed or legal. Footing: [L1] John 4:24 "God is a Spirit" with [L3] Luke 24:39 "a spirit hath not flesh and bones," [L2] ἐνομίζετο (*enomizeto*, "was supposed") in [L1] Luke 3:23, and [L3] Luke 2:49.
5. The child's flesh came from Mary and his Davidic descent is bodily through her. Footing: [L1] Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman" with [L2] ἐκ γυναικός (*ek gynaikos*, "out of a woman"), [L1] Romans 1:3 with [L2] σπέρματος (*spermatos*, "seed"), and [L3] Jeremiah 22:30.
6. Answer to the question: Christ had no biological father. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 and [L1] Luke 1:34-35 with [L2] ἐκ (*ek*, "out of") and ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω (*andra ou ginōskō*, "a man I know not"), carried by links 1 to 5 [L4].

# CHALLENGE: Joseph, the husband named in the record, is the father of the seed

The defender's chain runs D1 to D5 and closes on D6, "Christ had no biological father." I press each link with its own verses, read at the word level and in context. I then lay out the counter-chain the text builds, precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10).

---

## PRESS ON D1: Matthew 1:16, the passive and the husband

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verse that turns to the passive *egennēthē* (G1080, "was born") with *ex hēs* (feminine, "of whom") also names Joseph as *anēr* (G435, "husband"). The mother is named as the one who bore. The husband stands in the same verse.

**[L3]** "Born of" a woman is said of a man whose father is named. Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist." John's father is named at Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John."

**[L3]** The writer's very next address to Joseph names his line. Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

**[L4]** The footings are the passive with its named husband [L2, Matthew 1:16] and the "born of women" usage of a fathered man [L3, Matthew 11:11 with Luke 1:13]. A passive with the mother as source speaks of a fathered child elsewhere in the same Gospel. So the change of verb at 1:16 states the birth from the mother, and the line Matthew writes, a "begat" line (Matthew 1:12, "Jechonias begat Salathiel"), ends at "Joseph the husband of Mary." The verse fits a named father. The defender's "legal line" is a category Matthew 1:2-16 does not use.

---

## PRESS ON D2: the timing rows read in Matthew's own order

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband..." **[L1]** Matthew 1:24: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife."

**[L2]** *synelthein* (G4905, "to come together") is set by what Matthew narrates next: "took unto him his wife" (1:24), her coming into his house.

**[L3]** The law names that same step as a distinct act after betrothal. Deuteronomy 20:7: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" The law also calls the betrothed damsel a wife. Deuteronomy 22:24: "he hath humbled his neighbour's wife."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *ouk eginōsken autēn heōs hou eteken* ("knew her not till she brought forth") carries the abstinence up to the birth. In Matthew's order it follows the taking of 1:24.

**[L4]** The footings are Matthew's sequence [L1, 1:18, 1:24, 1:25] and the law's two steps, betrothed and then taken [L3, Deuteronomy 20:7], with *synelthein* [L2]. Three things follow:
- Matthew 1:18 dates the finding before the taking into his house.
- Matthew 1:25 covers the time after the taking.
- Joseph is "her husband" (1:19) and she is "Mary thy wife" (1:20) from the espousal.

The defender's link joins 1:25 to the time before 1:24, and Matthew's order does not join them.

**On "of the Holy Ghost" (*ek*):**
- **[L2]** Matthew 1:20's margin gives *gennaō*, "begotten."
- **[L3]** The same *ek* with the same verb is said of believers. 1 John 5:1: "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." John 1:13 says of believers: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."
- **[L4]** Both of those verses use *ek* with God for covenant origin, said of men who have fathers. The row that carries "of the Holy Ghost" names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife" in the same sentence. It fits the named father.

---

## PRESS ON D3: Luke 1:34-35 at the word level

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *andra ou ginōskō* is present active indicative, "I do not know." It states her condition when the angel spoke, a virgin "espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27, *parthenos*). The word names her state at the annunciation.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2] and [L3]** The two verbs, at their other rows:
- *eperchomai* (G1904, "come upon"). Acts 1:8: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me." These are the apostles, empowered.
- *episkiazō* (G1982, "overshadow"). Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them." Acts 5:15: "that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them."

**[L4]** At those rows [L3] the same verbs [L2] are empowerment and presence. The defender's "excludes a man's contribution" makes these verbs supply a begetting, and they supply that nowhere else.

**The "therefore" (*dio kai*).** The *dio kai* in verse 35 connects back to verse 32, not forward to biological divine paternity.
- **[L1]** Luke 1:32, given before Mary's question: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- **[L3]** The title's source names a son with a man for his father. 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son." 1 Chronicles 28:6 gives the son David begat and God's title in one verse: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father."
- **[L3]** Psalm 2:7, "Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee," is applied in the New Testament on three occasions:
  - the resurrection, Acts 13:33: "he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee";
  - the priesthood, Hebrews 5:5: "Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee";
  - beside 2 Samuel 7:14, Hebrews 1:5: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?"

**Isaiah 7:14.**
- **[L2]** The Hebrew is *ha-almah* (H5959, "the young woman"). The defender's own witness shows the difference. Genesis 24:43 uses *almah*. Genesis 24:16, where Moses states virginity, uses *bethulah* (H1330, "virgin") and adds "neither had any man known her."
- **[L3]** Isaiah's sign is bounded in Isaiah's day. Isaiah 7:16: "before the child shall know to refuse the evil, and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings." Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. [went: Heb. approached]"
- **[L4]** Matthew's application stands (Matthew 1:23). The prophecy he applies [L1, Isaiah 7:14] is fulfilled in its own chapter by a conception through a man's approach [L3, Isaiah 8:3]. It fits a fathered child.

---

## PRESS ON D4: "a spirit hath not flesh," and the father Luke names

**[L1]** John 4:24, "God is a Spirit," with **[L3]** Luke 24:39, "a spirit hath not flesh and bones." I hold both as written.

**[L1] and [L2]** The flesh of the promised son is "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30). *osphys* (G3751) is "loins, procreative power."

**[L3]** The seed is in the father's loins. Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father."

**[L4]** A spirit hath not flesh [L1, L3]. The text places flesh-seed in a father's loins [L2, Acts 2:30; L3, Hebrews 7:10]. So the defender's own verses require the child's flesh to come from a man's loins.

**On Hebrews 10:5.** Hebrews 2:17 says how the body was prepared: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren." Hebrews 2:14: "he also himself likewise took part of the same."

**On Luke 3:23.**
- **[L2]** *enomizeto* (G3543) is the same form as Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made." The word means custom, and it carries no verdict of its own.
- **[L3]** Joseph and Mary themselves are "supposing" at Luke 2:44: "they, supposing him to have been in the company."

**On Luke 2:49.**
- **[L1]** The defender misquotes it. The KJV reads "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" (Luke 2:49), with a capital F.
- **[L3]** Luke 2:51 follows: "And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them."
- **[L4]** One child has God as Father and David as father in one verse [L3, 1 Chronicles 28:6]. Mary's "thy father" [L1, Luke 2:48] stands beside "my Father's business" as Solomon's two fathers stand together.

**On the narrator's usage.**
- **[L1]** Luke's narrator writes "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41).
- **[L3]** The town says: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42).
- **[L3]** A disciple says: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).

---

## PRESS ON D5: the line runs by the father's house

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."

**[L1] and [L3]** Mary's one named kin is Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth." She is "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5).

**[L1] and [L2]** The reckoning is Numbers 1:18, "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." *beit avotam* is *bayith* (H1004, "house") with *'ab* (H1, "father").

**[L3]** The register struck the house called after a wife. Ezra 2:61-62: "the children of Barzillai; which took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name: These sought their register [among] those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."

**I put the question to the defender:** Hebrews 7:14 says "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." Given the law of Numbers 1:2 and 1:18, "by the house of their fathers," how is it evident?

**On Jeremiah 22:30.**
- **[L1]** Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless." Yet Matthew 1:12 says "Jechonias begat Salathiel."
- **[L3]** The signet plucked at Jeremiah 22:24 is given again at Haggai 2:23: "O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel... will make thee as a signet." Jeremiah's own rule is 18:8: "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil."
- **[L4]** The defender's D5 itself gives "the throne of his father David" through Joseph [L1, Luke 1:32]. A curse that bars Joseph's line would bar that throne equally. The defender's reading of the curse cuts its own D5.

**On Galatians 4:4.**
- **[L1]** "made of a woman."
- **[L3]** It uses the mortality idiom. Job 14:1: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days, and full of trouble."

---

## THE COUNTER-CHAIN

**C1. The seed comes out of a man's body.**
- **[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- **[L1]** Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]"
- **[L2]** *zera'* (H2233, "seed, posterity") and *osphys* (G3751, "loins").
- **[L3]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**C2. The father is named.**
- **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- **[L3]** John 6:42 and John 1:45, quoted above, and Luke 4:22: "Is not this Joseph's son?"

**C3. Joseph and Mary are husband and wife, and begetting is by knowing.**
- **[L1]** Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:19 calls him "Joseph her husband," Matthew 1:20 calls her "Mary thy wife," and Deuteronomy 22:24 calls the betrothed "his neighbour's wife."
- **[L2]** *heōs hou* ("till") at Matthew 1:25 bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy.
- **[L4]** On these footings, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

**C4. "Son of God" is a covenant title.**
- **[L1]** Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead."
- **[L3]** 1 Chronicles 28:6, quoted above.
- **[L2]** *horisthentos* (margin "Gr. determined").

**C5. Conclusion [L4].** C1 through C4 together answer the topic: Christ had a biological father, Joseph, of the house of David.

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES (the defender's links lack footing)

**LINK D1.** "So the genealogy is a legal line through Joseph and not a claim of generation by him."
ASSUMES: Matthew's line is a legal line. ROWS GIVE: "Jechonias begat Salathiel" (Matthew 1:12) and "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary" (Matthew 1:16), a begat line ending at the husband.

**LINK D2.** "So no male act of Joseph's, nor any other man's, entered the conception."
ASSUMES: the coming together of Matthew 1:18 is the first knowing of husband and wife. ROWS GIVE: "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24), the taking into his house, and "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19), husband from the espousal.

**LINK D3.** "So the angel's answer excludes a man's contribution by what it supplies in place of one."
ASSUMES: the Holy Ghost's coming upon is a supply of seed. ROWS GIVE: "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses" (Acts 1:8), the same verb as empowerment.

**LINK D4.** "The child corrects the term "father" and applies it to God." and "Joseph's "fatherhood" is legal and reputed. It is not biological."
ASSUMES: Luke 2:49 corrects Mary. ROWS GIVE: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" (Luke 2:49), followed by "was subject unto them" (Luke 2:51), and "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him [to be] my son" (1 Chronicles 28:6), two fathers held in one verse.

**LINK D5.** "The Holy Ghost is not a David descendant, so the descent must come through the mother." and "That resolves the apparent conflict only if the flesh came from Mary."
ASSUMES: Mary is of the house of David. ROWS GIVE: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27); "he was of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4); Mary's cousin Elisabeth "of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5, 1:36).

**LINK D6 (keystone).** "Answer to the question: Christ had no biological father."
ASSUMES: links D1 to D5 stand. ROWS GIVE: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ" (Acts 2:30); "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48); "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42).

# ROUND 2: Defender's answer to the presses and to the unsupported-L4 list

I take the challenger's presses in order. I concede where a link floats, and I show footing where it stands.

---

## CORRECTIONS AND CONCESSIONS

1. **Luke 2:49.** The KJV reads "my Father's business", with a capital F. My opening quoted it with a lowercase f, and I own the slip. The point does not rest on the capital. It rests on the contrast between "thy father" and "my Father's" inside one exchange (see D4 below).
2. **Genesis 24:43 and *almah*.** I conceded that H5959 *almah* (young woman of marriageable age) does not by itself state virginity. The challenger is right that Genesis 24:16 uses H1330 *bethulah* (virgin) for that. I withdraw the lexical claim as load-bearing. The virgin-conception footing rests on G3933 *parthenos* (virgin) at Matthew 1:23 and Luke 1:27, and on Luke 1:34.
3. **D2 and *synelthein*.** The challenger's order is accepted: the finding in Matthew 1:18 comes before the taking in Matthew 1:24. G4905 *synerchomai* (to come together, to cohabit conjugally) is not the hinge. The footing moves to Matthew 1:19-20, below.
4. **D5, "legal succession through Joseph".** I withdraw that phrase from Luke 1:32. D5 now stands on Mary's descent, with Jeremiah 22:30 as a supporting row only.

---

## ANSWER ON D1: Matthew 1:16

**[L1]** Matthew 1:3: "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar". **[L1]** Matthew 1:5: "Booz begat Obed of Ruth".

**[L2]** G1080 *gennaō* is "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)". In Matthew 1:3 and 1:5 the mother is named, yet the father stays the subject of the active *egennēsen* (begat). Naming a mother does not remove the father's verb.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus".

**[L2]** At the last link the active verb passes to Jacob and Joseph. The birth of Jesus is the passive *egennēthē* (was born) with *ex hēs*, "out of whom" (feminine singular). No man is the subject of "begat" for Jesus.

D3 vs C3 (Luke 1:35): UNDERDETERMINED -- Luke 1:35 gives the Holy Ghost as the overshadowing power answering Mary's lack of knowing a man, while the titles themselves carry covenant echoes across Davidic promises -- GROUND: Luke 1:35 grounds divine sonship in the Holy Ghost's coming upon Mary while fulfilling covenant promises given to David.
D4 vs C4 (Luke 3:23): UNDERDETERMINED -- Luke 3:23 qualifies Joseph's parenthood with "as was supposed" in the genealogy, while Luke 2:48 records Mary speaking of "thy father" according to custom -- GROUND: The common reckoning of Joseph as father in civic usage stands alongside the textual qualification of reputed descent.
D5 vs C5 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3 declare Christ made of David's seed according to the flesh, which the texts do not explicitly trace through a named maternal genealogy -- GROUND: Scripture affirms Davidic descent according to the flesh while registering tribal lines through fathers' houses.
D6 vs C6 (Hebrews 2:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Hebrews 2:14 affirms partaking of flesh and blood like the children, which Defender grounds in the human mother and Challenger in paternal generation -- GROUND: Partaking of flesh and blood defines human nature without specifying the biological necessity of a human male parent.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no biological human father

**Position.** "Biological father" means a male parent who supplies the seed of the child's conception. The KJV text says the child's conception was *of the Holy Ghost*, within a virgin, with no man involved. Joseph was husband, legal father and guardian, but not begetter.

## 1. The text states the mode of conception

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *sunerchomai* (G4905), "to come together," is the verb for the couple's union. The text places the conception before that union. *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537 + G4151 + G40), "out of the Holy Ghost," gives the source of the pregnancy with the preposition *ek*, "out of," marking origin.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *to gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), "that which is begotten or conceived," is the same root used for the human "begats" of Matthew 1. Here the begetting is attributed to the Holy Ghost, not to a man.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the conception before any union with Joseph. Matthew 1:20, through *gennaō* with *ek*, assigns the origin of the conceived child to the Holy Ghost. So no human male is the origin of the child, which excludes a biological human father. This rests on two [L1] verses and two [L2] grounds.

## 2. Mary's own testimony and the angel's answer

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," is used here of sexual knowledge. *anēr* (G435) is "a man," a male. Mary is betrothed, so the question concerns the manner of conception, not the future.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *episkiazō* (G1982), "to overshadow," and *eperchomai* (G1904), "to come upon," describe divine action. *dio kai* (G1352), "therefore also," makes the divine action the stated reason for the title.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Mary is called a virgin before the angel speaks.

**[L4]** The angel answers "how" with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, not with a man. Luke 1:27 says she was a virgin and Luke 1:34 says she knew no man. Together these show the angel's answer replaces human paternity. A biological father would not need "therefore" to ground the title.

## 3. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern

# Link round: the defender's answers

The challenger's list carries its verses under "ROWS GIVE", not under a "PRESSED WITH" label (ruling 392). I answer every one of them anyway, quoting each.

## LINK D1: SUPPORTED

**Challenger's rows:** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God" (1 John 5:1); "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3); "Joseph, thou son of David … Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** G1064 *gastēr*, "belly, womb," stands in the Greek of "with child." The conception is therefore a literal pregnancy in the womb. G4905 *synerchomai* is "come together … or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)." In Matthew 1:24 the "taking" is G3880 *paralambanō*, "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself." Matthew uses two different verbs. The challenger equates them without a row.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Joseph knew her not before the finding (1:18, before they came together). He knew her not after it (1:25). The challenger's own bounding of 1:25 to "the pregnancy after the taking" leaves the conception in the one gap where 1:18 says there was no coming together.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 (*synerchomai*, conjugal union, after the finding) and Matthew 1:25 (no knowing till the birth) together leave no union of Joseph and Mary before the birth. A conception "of the Holy Ghost" in that womb therefore has no human begetter beside it.

**On 1 John 5:1 and John 1:13.**

**[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

**[L2]** G1080 *gennaō* carries "figuratively, to regenerate" in its range. 1 John 5:1 is a regeneration of those who "believeth." Matthew 1:20 is a "conceived in her."

**[L3]** John 1:13 itself uses *ek* ("of") with God to exclude "the will of man" as the origin. The challenger's own row therefore shows *ek theou* ("of God") marking the origin as not human.

**[L4]** The figure of 1 John 5:1 is carried by its context of faith. The context of Matthew 1:18-20 is a womb, a betrothal and an unbroken "knew her not." John 1:13 and Matthew 1:25 are footings; the figure cannot be carried across into a literal pregnancy.

**On Romans 1:3.**

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L2]** The verb is G1096 *ginomai*, "made, become." It is the same verb Paul uses of Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman." It is not *gennaō*, "begat."

**[L3]** Romans 9:5: "and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ [came]."

**[L4]** "According to the flesh" marks descent from David and from Israel. It names the race, not a male parent. Luke 3:31 supplies a second line (see D6).

## LINK D2: SUPPORTED

**Challenger's rows:** "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David" (Luke 1:32); "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses" (Acts 1:8); "Solomon thy son … I have chosen him [to be] my son" (1 Chronicles 28:6).

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** G4459 *pōs*, "in what way?", asks the manner. G1904 *eperchomai* is "to supervene, i.e. arrive … (figuratively) influence." G1982 *episkiazō* is "to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence." The challenger rightly cites Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 as power and presence. That is divine action on persons, and no man's act appears in either verb.

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** "Biological father" means a male who begets by natural generation. The KJV text says Jesus Christ was conceived in Mary, a virgin, by the Holy Ghost, with no man involved. Joseph was her husband and the child's supposed father in law and in public reckoning. He was not the one who begot him.

## 1. Mary was with child before any union with a man

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] "Found with child" is *en gastri echousa* (G1722, G1064, G2192), literally "having in womb". The phrase "before they came together" (*prin ē synelthein*, G4250, G4905) puts the conception before any union of husband and wife.
[L3] Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". Luke 1:34 records her own words: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L2] "Know" is *ginōskō* (G1097), the Greek counterpart of Hebrew *yada'* (H3045). That Hebrew word is the sexual idiom in Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain."
[L4] Luke 1:34 uses the idiom of Genesis 4:1 and stands beside Matthew 1:18's "before they came together". So the conception is placed before any union, and the question "How?" is put by a woman who has known no man. No human male stands behind the conception.

## 2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] "Of" is *ek* (G1537), meaning "out of", the preposition of source. "Conceived" is *gennēthen* (G1080, *gennaō*), the verb of begetting. Its source is *pneumatos hagiou* (G4151, G40), "Spirit holy". The verb that elsewhere names a father's act is here given the Spirit as its source.
[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
[L2] "Overshadow" is *episkiazō* (G1982), "to cast a shade upon". The power of the Highest is the agent, and "therefore" (*dio*, G1352) makes that agency the reason for the title "Son of God".
[L4] Matthew 1:20 names the source of the begetting (*ek*, G1537, with *gennaō*, G1080). Luke 1:35 names the agent and the consequence ("therefore"). The text therefore gives a divine agent in the place a human begetter would occupy, and gives no human begetter.

## 3. Joseph's fatherhood is stated as supposed, not as begetting

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
[L2] Through verses 2–15 the genealogy repeats *egennēsen* (G1080, active), "begat". At verse 16 it changes to *egennēthē* (passive), "was born". The relative "of whom" is *hēs* (G3739, feminine singular), so it refers to Mary alone and cannot refer to Joseph. Joseph is called *anēr* (G435), "husband", and the line does not say "Joseph begat Jesus".
[L3] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph". [L2] "Supposed" is *nomizō* (G3543), "to deem by custom or law", which marks an opinion held by others.
[L4] Matthew 1:16 breaks the pattern of "begat" at exactly the point where Jesus is named, and uses a feminine relative. Luke 3:23 labels Joseph's sonship as a supposition. The two together show that Joseph's relation to the child is that of husband of the mother and legal father, not begetter.

## 4. The testimony of the law and the prophets agrees: the woman, not a man

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
[L2] "Virgin" is *'almah* (H5959), a young woman of marriageable age.
[L3] Genesis 24:43 uses the same word for Rebekah, and Genesis 24:16 says of her "a virgin, neither had any man known her".
[L3] Matthew 1:23 quotes the prophecy with *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin": "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."
[L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed". The deliverer is called the woman's seed, in a verse that speaks of no man.
[L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
[L2] "Made" is *ginomai* (G1096, *genomenon*), and "of a woman" is *ek gynaikos* (G1135). The origin named is the woman alone, and the verse mentions no man's part.
[L4] Isaiah 7:14 gives the sign as a virgin conceiving. Genesis 24:16 and 24:43 show that *'almah* (H5959) is used of a woman no man had known. Matthew 1:23 renders it *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin". Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 name only the woman as origin. Together these show that the prophetic sign, its Greek rendering and the apostle's wording all fit one account: a woman who had known no man bore the child.

## 5. Answering the likely objections

**Luke 2:48.** [L1] "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Here Mary uses the household's language for the man who is her husband and the child's guardian.
[L3] The child's reply in Luke 2:49 is "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" The child redirects the word "father" to another.
[L4] Luke 2:48 is a speech of ordinary usage, and Luke 2:49 corrects its referent. Both are consistent with Luke 3:23's "as was supposed".

**John 6:42.** [L1] "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" This is the speech of unbelievers, and they say what they suppose.
[L3] Luke 3:23 ("as was supposed") is the narrator's own label for that supposition.
[L4] The objection reports a public opinion that the narrator's own words in Luke 3:23 mark as supposed, so it does not establish begetting.

**Matthew 1:25.** [L1] "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." [L2] The verb *ginōskō* (G1097), "knew", is the same idiom as Genesis 4:1's *yada'* (H3045). The text says Joseph did not know her until she had borne the child, so he cannot be the begetter of that birth.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Mary was with child before any union with Joseph and had known no man. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost"; [L1] Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man"; [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, "know") with [L3] Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived".
2. The text names the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception, not a man. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"; [L2] *ek* (G1537, "out of") with *gennaō* (G1080, "begotten"); [L3] Luke 1:35, "the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God".
3. Joseph is husband and supposed father, not begetter. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16, "Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus"; [L2] *hēs* (G3739, feminine "of whom") after the repeated *egennēsen* (G1080, "begat"); [L3] Luke 3:23, "as was supposed the son of Joseph", with *nomizō* (G3543, "deemed by custom").
4. The prophecy and the apostle name only the woman as origin. Footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14, "a virgin shall conceive"; [L2] *'almah* (H5959, "young woman of marriageable age") with *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin"); [L3] Galatians 4:4, "made of a woman", and Genesis 24:16, "neither had any man known her".
5. Christ had no biological father: no human male begot him, and he was conceived in a virgin by the Holy Ghost. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20, "of the Holy Ghost"; [L2] *ek* (G1537) as source and *parthenos* (G3933) as the mother's state; [L3] Luke 1:35 and Matthew 1:25, "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".

# Round 2: link round and answer to the challenger's chain

The challenger's seven premises are answered in order. Where a premise floats free, I say so. Every pressed verse is quoted under its premise.

---

## LINK 1: SUPPORTED
*Premise: "No human male stands behind the conception."*

**Pressed with:** Luke 1:31, Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:24, Genesis 4:1.

[L1] Luke 1:31: "And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS."
[L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
[L2] *pōs* (G4459) is "an interrogative particle of manner; in what way?". Mary asks the way of the conception. *ginōskō* (G1097) is "know". The challenger's C3 grants that this is the knowing of Genesis 4:1, "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived".
[L4] Luke 1:31 puts the conception after the angel's word. Luke 1:34 asks by what way it will come to a woman who knows no man. Luke 1:35, the angel's answer, names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as the way. If Joseph's taking, Matthew 1:24 "took unto him his wife", were the way, the answer would name it. It names another agent. So Mary's state in verse 34 is the state in which the conception is promised, and verse 35 supplies its means.

The challenger's chain has Joseph know Mary "within the espousal". Three rows stand against that.

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] *synerchomai* (G4905) is, in the lexicon's words, "specially, cohabit (conjugally)". The finding is placed before conjugal cohabitation.
[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
[L3] Deuteronomy 22:24, the challenger's own row, has the penalty fall on "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife". Joseph took the pregnancy for another man's doing.
[L4] A husband who had known his wife would have no ground to put her away over her pregnancy. Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph did not count the child his, and Deuteronomy 22:24 shows what a pregnancy in a betrothed woman signified. So C3's step "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal" has no row and is contradicted by Matthew 1:18-19. Being "wife" (Matthew 1:20, "Mary thy wife") is a legal status. It does not state that knowing took place.

## LINK 2: SUPPORTED
*Premise: "The text therefore gives a divine agent in the place a human begetter would occupy, and gives no human begetter."*

**Pressed with:** Matthew 1:20, 1 John 5:1, Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, Acts 5:15, Luke 1:32.

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
[L2] *gennēthen* (G1080) is "to procreate (properly, of the father...)". The KJV margin reads "begotten". The object is "that which is conceived in her", the thing in the womb.
[L4] The angel gives the Holy Ghost as the reason Joseph need not fear. Joseph is addressed as "son of David", the man who might be taken for the cause, and is told the source lies elsewhere. The challenger reads the verse whole; read whole, it answers Joseph's fear about whose doing the pregnancy was (Matthew 1:19). The reason is: not yours, of the Holy Ghost.

**1 John 5:1.** [L1] "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him."
[L2] The same lexicon marks *gennaō* (G1080) as "figuratively, to regenerate". In 1 John 5:1 the subject is a believer already living, who is regenerated, and the verse names his human begetter separately ("him that begat"). In Matthew 1:20 the object is the thing being conceived in the womb, so the verb marks the origin of the conceiving itself. I grant that *ek* with *gennaō* of God does not by itself prove the absence of a father. The proof is Matthew 1:20 read with 1:18-19.

**Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, Acts 5:15.**
[L1] Acts 1:8: "the Holy Ghost is come upon you". [L1] Luke 9:34: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them". [L1] Acts 5:15: "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them".
[L2] *eperchomai* (G1904) is "to supervene... (figuratively) influence". *episkiazō* (G1982) is "to invest with preternatural influence".
[L4] I grant that these words name influence and presence. The question is what Luke 1:35 puts the influence on. It is on Mary, in answer to "How shall this be", with the result "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". In Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34 and Acts 5:15 no conception is in view. In Luke 1:35 the influence is the stated way of the conception. That is the agent in the begetter's place.

**The "therefore" and Luke 1:32.**
[L1] Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
[L2] *dio kai* (G1352 with G2532) is "wherefore also".
[L4] In Luke 1:35 the "therefore" follows, in the same verse, the clauses "shall come upon thee" and "shall overshadow thee". Verse 32 gave the title and verse 35 gives its ground, which the "also" marks. A ground may follow a title already given. [L2] *patēr* (G3962) is "father (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)". David is called "his father" in Luke 1:32 though many generations removed. So "father" in that verse names the line, not a begetter.

## LINK 3: SUPPORTED
*Premise: "Joseph's relation to the child is that of husband of the mother and legal father, not begetter."*

**Pressed with:** Acts 16:13, Luke 2:44, Luke 2:48, Luke 2:27, Luke 2:33.

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".
[L2] *nomizō* (G3543) is "to do by law (usage)... by extension, to deem or regard: suppose, think, be wont". The word has two senses. Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made", uses the "wont" sense.
[L1] Luke 2:44: "supposing him to have been in the company".
[L3] Luke 2:46, "they found him in the temple". The challenger's own witness for this verb shows a supposition that was mistaken, since he was not in the company.
[L4] Which sense stands in Luke 3:23 is settled by its place. The word is inserted in parenthesis, and it qualifies only the first link of a list that otherwise runs "which was [the son] of". With the sense "wont", the parenthesis would have nothing to qualify. With the sense "deem", it marks the narrator's distance from the common view. This agrees with Matthew 1:16, which gives *anēr* (G435) "husband" and a feminine "of whom" in place of "begat".

[L1] Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
[L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
[L2] *patēr* (G3962) stands in both verses with two referents. The challenger grants "two registers" and says Luke 2:49 names the covenant father. The register of Luke 2:48 is the household's. The register of biology is not decided by the household's word. Matthew 1:20 decides it.

[L1] Luke 2:27: "when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him after the custom of the law". The act is a legal one.
[L1] Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled". [L4] The narrator, in the very scene the challenger presses, writes "Joseph and his mother", not "his father and mother".

## LINK 4: SUPPORTED, in narrowed form
*Premise: "Genesis 24:16 and 24:43 show that 'almah (H5959) is used of a woman no man had known."*

**Pressed with:** Proverbs 30:19, Genesis 24:16, Isaiah 8:3.

[L1] Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]". [L1] Genesis 24:16: "a virgin, neither had any man known her".
[L3] Genesis 24:45: "behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder". The woman whom 24:16 describes is the one who answers the 'almah (H5959) description of 24:43.
[L4] I grant that H5959 does not itself state virginity. Proverbs 30:19, "the way of a man with a maid", shows the word is general. My claim narrows to this: the word is applied to a woman of whom the text says no man had known her, so it fits the sign.

What carries the sign is the following.
[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "the Lord himself shall give you a sign". [L2] *'oth* (H226) is sign. [L3] Isaiah 7:11: "Ask thee a sign of the LORD thy God; ask it either in the depth, or in the height above."
[L1] Isaiah 8:3: "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son." The prophetess's conception was by approach, and her son was named Mahershalalhashbaz, not Immanuel.
[L1] Matthew 1:22: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled". [L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child". [L2] *parthenos* (G3933) is virgin.
[L4] A sign of the depth or the height is not an ordinary conception, so Isaiah 8:3 does not fit it. "All this was done" in Matthew 1:22 takes in the conception of 1:18-20, and 1:23 names the virgin as the one "with child". So the fulfilled sign sets the virgin at the conception, not only at the announcement.

## LINK 5: CONCEDED
*Premise: "Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 name only the woman as origin."*

**Pressed with:** Matthew 11:11, Luke 1:13, Genesis 4:25.

[L1] Matthew 11:11: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist". [L1] Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". [L1] Genesis 4:25: "And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son... another seed instead of Abel".
These three show that "of a woman" and "her seed" are said of children who had human fathers. By themselves they do not exclude a father. I withdraw Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 as load-bearing for the exclusion. Link 4 stands on Isaiah 7:11, 7:14 and Matthew 1:22-23, which I have exhibited above.

## LINK 6: SUPPORTED
*Premise: "Christ had no biological father: no human male begot him."*

**Pressed with:** Romans 1:3, Acts 2:30, Luke 2:4, Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:24.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh". [L2] *spermatos* (G4690) is seed. *ginomai* (G1096) is "made, come into being". The verse states descent from David. It does not say whether the last link is a man or a woman.
[L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ". [L2] *osphys* (G3751) is loins.
[L1] Hebrews 7:10: "he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." [L3] Hebrews 7:9: "Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham."
[L4] The challenger's own row about loins is Hebrews 7:10. There Levi was in the loins of Abraham, who is not Levi's begetter, since Jacob stood between them. So "loins" names descent through a line of generations. Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 therefore require descent from David, and Matthew 1:16, "of whom was born Jesus", gives that descent through the mother. The seed rows do not require a human begetter at the last step. Acts 2:30 also says God "would raise up Christ".

[L1] Luke 2:4: Joseph "was of the house and lineage of David". I grant this. Joseph is Davidic, and Matthew 1:20 calls him "son of David". That makes the child heir in law by the taking and the naming.
[L3] The naming is not a father's act only. Luke 1:31 tells Mary "shalt call his name JESUS", and Genesis 4:25 says "she bare a son, and called his name Seth".

On the challenger's C2 chain, step 4:
[L1] Luke 1:36: "thy cousin Elisabeth". [L1] Luke 1:5: "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron".
[L4] A kinswoman of Aaron's line does not place Mary outside David. Kinship runs through either parent, and the challenger quotes no row that gives Mary's father's tribe. The step "so the Davidic line runs through Joseph" does not follow.
[L1] Ezra 2:61: the man "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name".
[L3] Numbers 1:18: "by the house of their fathers". This is a census of males, "from twenty years old and upward", and does not address a child with no human begetter. The challenger's own Ezra row shows that a name could be reckoned through a wife's father.

On C4:
[L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father". This is a choice made toward a son already begotten.
[L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". Here the source is of the conceiving itself.
[L1] Romans 1:4: "declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection". [L2] *horizō*, "determined", is the margin's word. Psalm 2:7 ("this day have I begotten thee") is applied to the day of declaration. Luke 1:35 places the title at the conception, "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The parallel to Solomon therefore fails, because Solomon had no such conception-source named.

## LINK 7: CONCEDED
*Premise: "so he cannot be the begetter of that birth" (from Matthew 1:25).*

**Pressed with:** Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:24, Matthew 1:25.

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." [L2] *heōs* (G2193) is "until, while". Read in the order of 1:18, 1:24 and 1:25, the "till" covers the time after the taking. It does not reach back to the conception.

I grant this. Matthew 1:25 alone bars a later union as the source and does not bar an earlier one. That inference from 1:25 alone floats free. The exclusion rests on Matthew 1:18 ("before they came together"), Matthew 1:19 (Joseph "minded to put her away"), Matthew 1:20 ("that which is conceived in her", already conceived before the taking of 1:24) and Luke 1:34-35. These were exhibited under Links 1 and 2.

---

## Standing summary

- The Holy Ghost is named as the source of the conception, and Mary asks the way and is answered with that source (Links 1 and 2).
- Joseph's fatherhood is marked as supposed, and the genealogy puts a husband where a begetter would stand (Link 3).
- The sign of Isaiah 7:14, as fulfilled in Matthew 1:22-23, places the virgin at the conception (Link 4, narrowed).
- The seed rows require descent from David and do not require a human begetter at the last step (Link 6).
- Conceded: Genesis 3:15 and Galatians 4:4 as stand-alone exclusions, and Matthew 1:25 as proof for the time before the taking.

The defender's keystone is D5: "Christ had no biological father: no human male begot him, and he was conceived in a virgin by the Holy Ghost." In round 2 the defender gave up two of its footings:

What remains rests on Matthew 1:18-20, Luke 1:34-35 and Luke 3:23. Each is answered below by the fit its rows show.

## 1. The timing rows, read in Matthew's own order (against D1)

The defender pressed Matthew 1:18-19 against the union. Here is how those rows fit the chain.

- **Matthew 1:18.** [L1] "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
  - [L2] *synerchomai* (G4905) is "to convene... come together... resort... (specially) cohabit." Matthew fixes what "came together" means by what follows.
  - [L3] Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife." Here [L2] *paralambanō* (G3880) is "to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself... take (unto, with)."
  - [L3] The law makes betrothal and taking two steps. Deuteronomy 20:7: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her? let him go and return unto his house."
  - [L4] Matthew 1:18 dates the *finding* before the taking into the house (1:24). Matthew 1:25 bounds the abstinence to the time after that taking, as the defender granted.

- **Matthew 1:19.** [L1] "Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
  - The verse states an intent and two grounds: his justness, and his unwillingness to expose her.
  - It names no other man. The defender's Deuteronomy 22:23-24 concerns "a man find her in the city, and lie with her." Matthew does not cite it.
  - [L3] The intent is answered in the next verse. Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"
  - The "for" grounds the command to *take her*. It points to the covenant claim on the child: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son" (2 Samuel 7:14).

- **The union, as the chain holds it.**
  - [L1] Genesis 4:1 is the defender's own footing: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."

## 2. Luke 1:35 at its own words (against D2)

- The defender reasoned that "If Joseph's taking... were the way, the answer would name it." That step argues from what the answer leaves unnamed.
- The fit the rows show runs back to the title.
  - [L1] Luke 1:32: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
  - [L2] The dio kai ("therefore") in v.35 connects back to v.32, not forward to biological divine paternity. The title and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.
- The verbs of v.35 are the verbs of empowerment and presence. The defender granted this.
  - *eperchomai* (G1904): "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you" (Acts 1:8).
  - *episkiazō* (G1982): "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them" (Luke 9:34).
- [L3] The pattern of the title is Solomon's. 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." One son has both the father who begat him and the God who names him son.
- The defender granted that *ek* with *gennaō* of God "does not by itself prove the absence of a father" (1 John 5:1). The phrase is therefore the covenant-origin marker. It stands in a row that names "Joseph, thou son of David."

## 3. Luke 3:23 and the household (against D3)

- [L2] *nomizō* (G3543) is "to do by law (usage)... be wont."
  - The same form stands at Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made."
  - At Luke 2:44 the same verb is used of Joseph and Mary themselves.
  - The verb carries no verdict of its own; its context decides.
- Luke's context names Joseph as father in his own narration and in Mary's mouth:
  - "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27)
  - "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41)
  - "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48)

## 4. The sign (against D4)

- [L2] Isaiah 7:14 has *'almah* (H5959), young woman: 7 verses, including "the way of a man with a maid" (Proverbs 30:19).
- Rebekah's virginity is stated by *bethulah* (H1330), with its own clause (Genesis 24:16).
- [L3] The sign is bounded in Ahaz's day:
  - "before the child shall know to refuse the evil" (Isaiah 7:16)
  - "And I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. [went: Heb. approached]" (Isaiah 8:3)
  - "before the child shall have knowledge to cry, My father, and my mother" (Isaiah 8:4)
  - "O Immanuel" (Isaiah 8:8)
- Matthew 1:23's *parthenos* (G3933) names Mary as Luke 1:27 does: "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David." That is her state at the announcement.

## 5. The seed and the loins (against D5)

- The defender read Hebrews 7:10 as descent "through a line of generations." The line it names is a line of fathers' loins:
  - [L1] Hebrews 7:10: "he was yet in the loins of his father."
  - [L3] Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham."
  - [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- The same line runs through Joseph:
  - Luke 1:27 and Luke 2:4 place "the house and lineage of David" on Joseph.
  - Luke 1:36 with Luke 1:5 gives Mary a kinswoman "of the daughters of Aaron."
- The defender cited Ezra 2:61 for reckoning through a wife's house. Ezra 2:62 records how that reckoning ended: "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- [L4] The chain:
  1. Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
  2. Acts 2:30 says "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh."
  3. *osphys* (G3751) is "procreative power."
  4. The house that carries David's line in these rows is Joseph's.
  5. So the seed comes through the named father, Joseph.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Jesus had no human biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed begot the child. My thesis is that the KJV text gives Jesus a mother, Mary, and a conception by the Holy Ghost. It gives him no man who begot him. Joseph was the husband of Mary and the one who named the child, but he was not the one who begot him.

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," and it happened before Mary and Joseph came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *Prin ē synelthein autous* (πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτούς) means "before they came together." *Synerchomai* (G4905) means to come together as a married couple. *Ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου) means "out of the Holy Spirit." The preposition *ek* (G1537) marks the source. The text therefore places the pregnancy before any union with Joseph and names its source as the Holy Ghost.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *Gennēthen* (γεννηθέν, from G1080 *gennaō*) means "begotten" or "conceived." In the same verse it is again paired with *ek pneumatos* (out of the Spirit). The angel gives the source of the begetting to Joseph in order to settle whether Joseph was the source.

**[L3]** Compare Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." If Joseph had begotten the child, there would have been nothing to resolve and no reason to put her away. The angel's words in 1:20 answer his doubt by naming a different source.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the coming together [L1, L2]. Matthew 1:19 shows that Joseph was troubled by it [L3]. Matthew 1:20 gives the Holy Ghost as the *ek* (source) [L2]. So the text excludes Joseph as the begetter.

## 2. Mary had not known a man, and Joseph "knew her not" until the birth

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Andra ou ginōskō* (ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω) means "I do not know a man." *Ginōskō* (G1097) is used here of marital knowledge. The present tense states her standing at the time of the announcement.

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." The Hebrew *yada* (H3045), to know, is the same idiom, and in that verse conception follows the knowing. Luke 1:34 uses the idiom in the negative, so no conception by man follows.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *Ouk eginōsken* (οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν) means "he was not knowing her." *Heōs hou* (ἕως οὗ) means "until which time." The imperfect tense marks continued abstinence through the whole period up to the birth.

**[L4]** Mary says she has not known a man [L1 Luke 1:34, L2 *ginōskō*]. The idiom for fathering is the same one used for Adam and Eve [L3 Genesis 4:1]. Joseph did not know her until the birth [L1 Matthew 1:25, L2 imperfect]. Therefore no man's seed was involved in the conception.

## 3. The angel states the mechanism and ties the child's title to it

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Epeleusetai* (ἐπελεύσεται) means "shall come upon." *Episkiasei* (ἐπισκιάσει) means "shall overshadow." *Dio kai* (διὸ καί) means "for which reason also," so the title rests on the conception. *Gennōmenon* (γεννώμενον) means "that which is being begotten." The child is "of thee" (*ek sou*), from Mary alone.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27 gives Mary's status: "to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary." The word is *parthenos* (G3933), virgin, at the point of the announcement.

**[L4]** The Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest are the named agents [L1, L2]. The child is "of thee," from Mary [L2]. The title "Son of God" is grounded in this by *dio kai* [L2]. The announcement is made to a *parthenos* [L3]. So the begetting was a miraculous act of God and not a union with a man.

## 4. Joseph is "husband" and "supposed" father, never the one who begat

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The genealogy before this verse uses *egennēsen* (ἐγέννησεν), "begat," in the active voice for each father in turn. At the end the pattern changes. Joseph is *ton andra Marias* (τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας), "the husband of Mary." The next verb is the passive *egennēthē* (ἐγεννήθη), "was born." The relative pronoun is *hēs* (ἧς), "of whom," in the feminine singular. Its only feminine antecedent is Mary, so Jesus is said to be born of her.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *Hōs enomizeto* (ὡς ἐνομίζετο) means "as was reckoned" or "as was supposed." *Nomizō* (G3543) is used of what is thought or assumed. Luke's wording marks the common opinion as differing from the fact.

**[L3]** Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled." The KJV gives the name Joseph here. Luke 2:49 supplies the child's own answer to Mary's "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48): "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" The child corrects the term "father."

**[L4]** The genealogy breaks its "begat" pattern at Joseph [L1, L2]. Luke records that the opinion was only "supposed" [L1, L2]. Luke 2:49 shows the child himself answering Mary's "thy father" with "my father's business" [L3]. So the references to Joseph as father are about legal standing and what people supposed.

## 5. Prophecy and the apostle's wording name only a woman

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** *Almah* (H5959) is the word for virgin. The same verse says it will be an *'oth* (H226), a sign, which would be no sign if it were an ordinary conception.

**[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses *almah* of Rebekah, and Genesis 24:16 describes her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her." Matthew 1:22-23 quotes the prophecy as fulfilled and renders *almah* as *parthenos* (G3933): "Behold, a virgin shall be with child."

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *Genomenon ek gynaikos* (γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός) means "come to be out of a woman." Only the woman is named as the source.

**[L4]** Isaiah's *almah* is a sign [L2]. It is the same word applied to a woman "neither had any man known her" [L3 Genesis 24:16, 24:43]. Matthew reads it as *parthenos* [L3 Matthew 1:22-23]. Paul names only the woman [L1, L2]. So the prophecy and the apostle's wording fit a conception without a human father.

## 6. Anticipated objections

- **"His parents" (Luke 2:41) and "thy father" (Luke 2:48).** **[L1]** Luke 2:41: "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year." **[L2]** *Goneis* (G1118) means "parents" and covers legal guardians, so it does not state who begat. **[L3]** Luke 2:49 answers Luke 2:48: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" **[L4]** Luke 3:23, which says "as was supposed" [L1, L2], gives the reading for such terms.
- **"Seed of David" (Romans 1:3).** The descent from David runs through Mary's line and through Joseph's legal standing. Matthew 1:16 names Mary as the one of whom Jesus was born [L1, L2].

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on:

1. The conception was out of the Holy Ghost before Mary and Joseph came together. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:20; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit), *prin ē synelthein* (before coming together), *gennēthen* (begotten); [L3] Matthew 1:19, Joseph's intent to put her away.
2. Mary had not known a man, and Joseph did not know her until after the birth. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:25; [L2] *ginōskō* (to know), *ouk eginōsken* (was not knowing, imperfect), *heōs hou* (until which time); [L3] Genesis 4:1, *yada* (to know) leads to conception.
3. The Holy Ghost coming upon her and the power of the Highest overshadowing her is the stated mechanism, and "Son of God" is grounded in it. # Round 2: the rows answer the challenge

I concede two points of footing first, because they are true. Then I answer the question put to me, and then each of the challenger's links.

## Concessions

**1. Genesis 24:16 stands on a different word.**
- [L1] Genesis 24:16: "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**2. Galatians 4:4 does not stand alone.**

- [L3] Job 14:1 ("Man [that is] born of a woman") and Matthew 11:11 use the same idiom of men who have fathers. So Galatians 4:4 states real human birth, and it supports my case without carrying it.

## The question put: how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda"?

- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L2] *Prodēlon* (G4271) means openly plain, evident. *Anatetalken* (from G393 *anatellō*) means has arisen or sprung up. The verse states where he arose from. It does not say a man of Judah begat him.

**The father's house, answered in two rows.**
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary."
- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli."
- [L2] In Luke 3:23 the line is carried by the bare genitive article *tou* (of the), with no verb of begetting. Matthew 1:16 uses *egennēsen* (begat).
- [L4] The same Joseph is given two fathers, Jacob and Heli. Matthew's verb *egennēsen* is a begetting [L2], while Luke's "of Heli" follows "as was supposed" and has no verb [L1, L2]. So the two lines are of two kinds. Matthew gives the legal line through the husband. Luke's line, which follows "as was supposed," is the one that runs through the household of Mary.
- I grant this is an inference. It stands on two layers, and DG-61 does not require a row to state it.

**The two houses.**
- Joseph's house is David's: Luke 2:4 ("of the house and lineage of David") and Matthew 1:20 ("Joseph, thou son of David").
- Joseph's act of naming the child is the legal step: [L1] Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS."
- [L2] *Parthenos* (G3933) in Luke 1:27 tells us only Mary's status. The tribe of Mary is not named there, so I rest nothing on that verse.

- [L4] Aaron's house is shown marrying into Judah [L3], and Luke 1:36 speaks only of kin [L1, L2]. So the rows do not close Mary's descent against Judah.
